behavior: Generally associated with rocks, but sometimes climbs into vegetation (agaves, palms, willows) or occurs on the ground among shrubs.
Eats insects, lizards and occasionally buds and fleshy fruits.
Lays 6-15 eggs May-July; probably buries eggs in the soil; inactive in cold and extreme heat.
habitat: Granite outcrops in chaparral and oak-covered slopes on the coastal side of southern California mountains, also yellow pine habitat.
On the desert side, rocky canyons and upper alluvial slopes with chaparral, palms or mesquite.
range: From the north side of San Gorgonio Pass (Peninsular Ranges, southern California) south to near La Paz in southern Baja California, including several Gulf of California islands; sea level to about 2,130 m.
